{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-sd-x","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"0452b343f7bb145afa16254c6d444c3e5467dcd4d1a39b5e21d5402f0aefa1e7","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-sd-class-std:lineage:14","source_registry_sha256":"a4e51960bfe4da242ea11046073ac8d3d0353ce120a5409a11c1f9ab4c4da57a","source_liveness_sha256":"1aea607665fc1312b9a6988c94545b32e414886d6d428b2b6d66e4261f9397f1"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Renewal, privileges, registration and responsibility","heading":"C — Knowledge dossier: Renewal, privileges, registration and responsibility","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Knowledge dossier: Renewal, privileges, registration and responsibility

FACT_ID: sec04-F01 | anchor: A12
The renewal section describes a license lasting 5 years and expiring on the holder’s birthday, except that a holder turning 21 has an expiration 30 days after that birthday. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec04-F02 | anchor: A12
Renewal is available up to 180 days before expiration unless the holder will be turning 21. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec04-F03 | anchor: A12
Renewing a South Dakota driver license requires a vision test. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec04-F04 | anchor: A12
When the license surrendered for renewal has expired, a knowledge test is required in addition to the vision test. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec04-F05 | anchor: A12
A foreign-country driver’s license duration is limited to the authorized stay documented by USCIS and cannot exceed 5 years. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec04-F06 | anchor: A12
The handbook says eligible people may use mail or online service for replacement and renewal once during any 10-year period. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec04-F07 | anchor: A12
The handbook states that online processing for license renewals, duplicates and restricted-minor-permit upgrades became available July 1, 2014. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec04-F08 | anchor: A12
A drug conviction involving a vehicle can be grounds for losing a South Dakota driver license. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec04-F09 | anchor: A12
A conviction for driving while intoxicated can cause loss of the driver license. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec04-F10 | anchor: A12
An alcohol conviction involving a minor can lead to loss of driving privileges. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec04-F11 | anchor: A12
Refusing an alcohol or drug test requested by a police officer can lead to license loss. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec04-F12 | anchor: A12
Driving during a court-ordered prohibition on driving can lead to license loss. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec04-F13 | anchor: A12
Driving while a license is suspended, cancelled, revoked or denied is a listed reason for losing driving privileges. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec04-F14 | anchor: A12
Providing false information in a driver-license or non-driver-identification application can cause license loss. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec04-F15 | anchor: A12
Leaving a financial judgment for motor-vehicle-crash damages unsettled can be grounds for license loss. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec04-F16 | anchor: A12
Attempting to change license information improperly or using another person’s license is a listed ground for license loss. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec04-F17 | anchor: A12
Failing to attend a reexamination requested by Driver Licensing can cause license loss. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec04-F18 | anchor: A12
Using a motor vehicle to commit a felony or causing a person’s death in a vehicle crash can lead to license loss. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec04-F19 | anchor: A12
Accumulating too many driving-record points under the applicable point system can cause license loss. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec04-F20 | anchor: A12
Failing to keep insurance proof for every owned vehicle or driving a vehicle without insurance proof can lead to license loss. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec04-F21 | anchor: A12
A traffic-violation conviction for conduct before age 16 can cause license loss for an instruction-permit or restricted-permit holder. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec04-F22 | anchor: A12
Not paying a fine imposed for a traffic-violation conviction can cause license loss. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec04-F23 | anchor: A12
Owing a South Dakota government agency at least $1,000 is a listed basis for license loss. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec04-F24 | anchor: A12
A driver younger than 18 can lose driving privileges after a conviction for violating the license restrictions. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec04-F25 | anchor: A12
The handbook lists arrest for a blood-alcohol concentration from 0.02 percent through 0.079 percent under SDCL 32-23-21 as a license-loss ground for a person under 21. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec04-F26 | anchor: A12
Selling or distributing alcohol to someone younger than 21 can cause license loss. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec04-F27 | anchor: A12
Possessing alcohol while under 21 can be a ground for license loss. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec04-F28 | anchor: A12
Eluding law enforcement is a listed ground for losing the driver license. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec04-F29 | anchor: A12
Revocation removes the driver license or the privilege to drive or apply for a license. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec04-F30 | anchor: A12
After revocation, the handbook requires the applicable tests, an application fee and a reinstatement fee in its stated $50 to $225 range. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec04-F31 | anchor: A12
The reinstatement discussion specifically requires vision and knowledge tests following revocation. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec04-F32 | anchor: A12
The printed in-person reinstatement schedule lists DWI fees of $100 for a first offense, $150 for a second and $200 for a third or later offense. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec04-F33 | anchor: A12
The printed in-person reinstatement schedule lists $125 for a second reckless-driving conviction within 1 year or for eluding an officer, $225 for vehicular battery or homicide, and $75 for other revocations. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec04-F34 | anchor: A12
Suspension removes the driver license or the privilege to drive or apply for a license. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec04-F35 | anchor: A12
After suspension, testing is unnecessary unless the license has expired, but the handbook requires an application fee and a $50 reinstatement fee. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0012]

Misconceptions: A suspension does not always require the tests required after revocation; an SR22 must come from the insurer to the central office. The no-points rule does not make speeding lawful.
Mnemonics: Use cause, credential, consequence and reinstatement as a retrieval cue; it adds no penalty or exemption.
Glossary: Revocation and suspension remove licensing or driving privileges; a registration certificate belongs in the vehicle, while the title is stored elsewhere; SR22 names the cited future-responsibility filing.
Dynamic facts: Printed fees and online-service eligibility require issuer refresh. Source conflict concerning minor permit-restriction sanctions is flagged for evidence review, without resolving it from outside knowledge.
